text:
The central conflict in the text revolves around the clash between economic greed and cultural preservation. Jacob, a prospector, discovers gold on sacred indigenous land, which immediately pits his personal gain against the local tribe's desire to protect their heritage. This internal and external struggle is intensified by the arrival of outsiders, forcing Jacob to confront a moral dilemma regarding his loyalties. He must choose between exploiting the resource for profit or respecting the indigenous people's rights and traditions.

The longest river in the world is the Nile River.
